articleTitle: Self-commissioning-a novel feature of modern inverter-fed induction motor drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: In practice, full use of the well-known advantages of modern AC drives with field-oriented control can only be made, if during commissioning the control system has been accurately adapted to the motor connected. In many applications, the parameters of the motor are not known beforehand. Therefore, special measurements and test runs had to be made during commissioning. Because of the sophisticated but also complicated structure of field-oriented control, setting the control parameters used to be a time-consuming procedure requiring specially trained staff. To simplify this adjustment, self-commissioning-a new feature of modern control systems-has been developed. The system itself determines the electrical parameters of the machine during commissioning and sets the control parameters accordingly. This is done at standstill. A test run follows to measure the inertia of the drive. The author describes this self-commissioning feature applied to a PWM inverter-fed asynchronous motor drive.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Online current monitoring for fault diagnosis in inverter fed induction motors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: There has been considerable research to develop new online monitoring techniques for detecting faults such as broken rotor bars or air gap eccentricity in induction motors. The author presents a set of current spectra which show that broken rotor bars or air-gap eccentricity can be detected in squirrel cage induction motors. The results are part of a long-term project on research into online diagnostic techniques for such motors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Four-quadrant brushless reluctance motor drive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Commutation of the SR motor is as simple as that of the brushless PM motor, using a similar shaft position sensor and gating logic. Speed and torque can be modulated by commutation angle control over a wide range. Combined with voltage p.w.m., sufficient flexibility is obtained by switching between a small number of modes or commutation angle combinations to at least double the speed and torque control ranges compared to those possible with fixed angles. Four-quadrant symmetrical operation is easily achieved, with extremely rapid reversing. The entire control is readily implemented using any of the normal methods (gate array, programmable logic array, custom LSI, or microprocessor).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The three-phase bridge rectifier with a capacitive load
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The 3-phase bridge rectifier supplying a capacitive load is significantly more difficult to analyse than the inductive load case. The authors examine how the ideal behaviour of such a system is affected by the following circumstances: (i) a supply impedance which includes resistance; (ii) less than infinite link capacitance; (iii) an unbalanced 3-phase supply. The authors derive results for a digital simulation (CAD) package, which conveniently illustrates the rectifier trends.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new method for the more accurate determination of conductor losses in power electronic converter magnetic components
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A set of analytical expressions has been derived which provide the means to analyse the AC resistance and losses in the windings of magnetic components. The equations are very versatile in that any periodic current waveform and three conductor types (solid wire, litz wire and strip conductors) can be accommodated. The experimental measurements seem to support the validity of these equations. The predictions are comparable to those of Butterworth's formulae for single layer coils. Measurements on a multi layer litz wire coil and on transformers with strip conductor, solid wire and litz wire windings also seem to support these equations. An important factor of the eddy current algorithm is the solution of the magnetic field. Already evident from the presented results, is a difference in the accuracy when curvature is ignored or incorporated during the calculation of losses in a long solenoid.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Innovative current sensing for brushless DC drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A method of deriving a motor current signal with a 3-phase inverter is described in which only the bus current and the inverter drive signals are required to determine motor current. The method may be applied without extra hardware to any multi-phase brushless DC drive, provided that no circulating currents are produced in the inverter. Therefore, transistors must be switched on and off in pairs and only two transistors may conduct at any time. This single resistor method eliminates the problem of balancing gains experienced with multi-sensor methods. The size advantages make it an ideal component of a controller designed for robotic or aerospace applications. However, some noise is injected into the current signal and the entire current loop requires careful design to ensure good inverter performance. To simplify description of the method, its operation in an H-bridge inverter is considered initially.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Field-orientation for controlling AC machines-principle and application
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author shows that, by introducing suitable moving coordinates, the control of AC machines can be made very simple. The principle of rotor or field orientation is based on the fact that only the component of the stator ampere turns the wave that is orthogonal to the rotor flux wave.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Increasing frequency using GTO in gate-assisted-turn-off mode
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The main advantage of GTO over thyristors is to reduce tq (turn-off time) to zero but at the cost of increasing Woff losses due to the tail current that sweeps residual stored charge off the thick N base while the voltage is restored across the device. Nevertheless, no significant improvement is obtainable if tq is much shorter than the carriers' life time in the N base, and auxiliary circuits' disposals, being considered equivalent for thyristors, are not equivalent in the case of GTO, some of them being dangerous for the device. To demonstrate this, a practical problem has been experienced with the aim of 25 kHz, 500 V, 230 A application. Four different GAT mode circuits (A, B, D, E), using the same 2 mu F capacitor as that used for the GTO mode, allowing approximately 4 mu s tq, have been tested (one shot Woff measurements at Tj=110 degrees C) and results have been compared to the losses of the GTO mode and of a thyristor mode (tq=8 mu s). Nine GTO and two thyristors have been cross tested that way.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A self oscillating bidirectional DC to DC converter employing minimum circuitry
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Self-oscillating push pull converters are ideally suited for the realisation of a 'DC transformer' where bidirectional power flow and DC voltage transformation at a fixed ratio is required. The major aims of this investigation are to use minimum circuitry and to determine the design criteria for efficient operation. Results on a 1.5 kW prototype indicated that high efficiencies are attainable, and the base drive circuit can be reduced to a minimum number of components, leading to low costs and improved reliability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of hysteresis modulation methods for VSI current control
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: An evaluation criterion of the current control methods for three phase voltage source inverters has been proposed. It refers to an ideal case, whose performances can be assumed as a limit the various solutions can be compared to. The criterion has been applied to some hysteresis control methods, showing that two of them give quite good steady state performances, which are near tot hat of the ideal case. This is in addition to excellent dynamic behaviour which is peculiar to the hysteresis methods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resonant high-frequency inverters using static induction transistors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors describe voltage-fed full bridge series resonant inverters using static induction transistors (SITs) which operate efficiently in the frequency range of 100 approximately 1000 kHz. The trial inverters are applied to 100 kHz and/or 400 kHz high power induction heating and melting power supplies. In addition, a quasi-resonant inverter suitable for radio-frequency applications is produced to diminish switching losses operating at 1 MHz. Both types of inverter are found to work safely with sufficiently high efficiency in feeding high output power.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Harmonic currents and torque pulsations with pulse width modulation methods in AC motor drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The pulse width modulation (PWM) method used in AC motor drives influences the harmonic current content and the torque pulsations. To investigate this, two PWM methods are compared by means of computer calculations and measurements on an 11 kW squirrel-caged induction motor fed by a transistor inverter. The investigated drive, with a deep-bar squirrel-caged standard induction machine which has frequency dependent rotor parameters, introduces some discrepancies between the measurements and the simulations. The PWM methods investigated are the natural sinusoidal modulation and the staircase modulation, which is a new uncomplicated and efficient modulation method. The same pulse number is used in both methods. To present a reference case, results with a quasi-square wave voltage are also being given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A bi-directional AC-DC power converter for fixed polarity DC loads
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Semiconductor power modules which include both transistors and diodes are extensively used for variable frequency inverters feeding motors, and they can also be used for the supply-side converter, providing rectification via the diodes and inversion via the transistors. The drawbacks are their cost, and supply waveform disturbances caused by transistor switching which is essential to the control of the inversion process. The use of an autotransformer (operating at supply frequency) to correct the voltage mismatch is possible but unattractive in terms of cost, and especially bulk. Other solutions, involving the isolation of the diode bridge during inversion by means of series transistors or thyristors, are possible, but involve transitional difficulties when power flow reverses. The authors describe a circuit which aims to solve these problems in an economical way involving minimum bulk and maximum controllability both in steady state and during transient operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Control of a neutral-point-clamped PWM inverter for high power AC traction drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Direct self-control used for a PWM invertor is particularly good with the torque and flux as controlled variables. The author uses direct self-control for a 3-level invertor for high power AC traction drives. Computer simulation shows that there is a good dynamic and steady state performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimisation of losses in PWM inverters
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: PWM inverters are now widely used for a range of applications which include AC motor drives and uninterruptible power supplies. Design techniques for them are quite well established and they are relatively reliable and efficient pieces of equipment. The authors deal with the losses that are produced in an inverter. There are two main sources of loss, namely on-state losses and switching losses, and the latter can be further divided into device losses and snubber resistor losses. It is not a simple matter to write down expressions for these losses, even for ideal conditions. The on-state losses in the transistors and diodes of an inverter are given, together with mathematical results for switching losses. An example of the breakdown of losses in a 25 kVA inverter is given, together with some discussion of methods by which the losses could be minimised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Resonant flyback switched-mode DC-DC converters using static induction power devices
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors present the state-of-the art series resonant DC-DC converters using static induction-transistors and thyristors, which are capable of operating in the switching frequency ranges from 50 kHz to 40 kHz. The circuit topologies of the two-switch quasi-resonant current-mode and the single-switch quasi-resonant voltage mode flyback converters are described. The new converters developed on the basis of the quasi-resonant forward converters include the more efficient switching processing at higher frequencies, low acoustic noise and reduced EMI, reduction of size and weight of energy-storage and resonant components and filter components, and effective utilization of parasitic L C components. The operating principles of both types of proposed flyback converters circuits using static induction power devices are explained, and the voltage regulation characteristics of the PFM or PWM time ratio control-based resonant flyback converters are illustrated and discussed in terms of the computer aided simulation results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power circuits for small permanent-magnet brushless DC drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Brushless DC drives incorporating motors with permanent-magnet excitation are being used in a rapidly-expanding range of applications, including the computer peripheral, automotive and machine tool industries. The overall dynamic torque producing capability of the drive is critically dependent on the interaction between the motor and power switching circuit. The authors examine various power circuit configurations and discuss their comparative merits, paying particular attention to the trade-offs between circuit complexity and overall drive performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A simple technique for modelling converters with indeterminate voltage states
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author describes a novel and simple technique for including the behaviour of the power electronic devices in motor drives. The method is simple to understand, and unlike the familiar primitive generalised machine approach, does not require transformation of the motor terminal conditions. The complete model for the drive system is represented in circuit form. This allows total flexibility and does not require any knowledge of the sometimes numerous modes of operation. The otherwise indeterminate motor voltage states are accounted for, and the true motor performance may be accurately predicted.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Study of power bidirectional switches using MOS-transistors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors compare three structures of bidirectional switches. They design low-cost control circuits without any sacrifice on standard features. The chosen switch is used in an AC-chopper whose characteristics are compared with a triac converter. The use of bidirectional switches simplifies the structures of static energy converters and increases performance.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A single-chip microcontroller based real-time PWM inverter
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors report on an investigation to develop a single-chip microcontroller based compact and versatile controller for inverter applications. A novel iterative generalized algorithm that, with a single program, computes switching angles, in real-time, for four sampling methods is used. Such an algorithm is implemented on an MCS-96 series microcontroller, whose high speed input output (HSIO) unit assures precise triggering of switching devices. The controller developed is robust, generates PWM waveforms of very high quality and is capable of tuning to its application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Switching behaviour of a pulse-commutated GTO
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The operation of an asymmetric (anode shorted) GTO is described theoretically and analysed experimentally. The interrelation between the turn-off losses and the turn-off time with the anode current, and the point of time where the negative gate voltage is applied, is presented. The influences of the snubber and gating circuit are also considered. It is shown that the anode shorted GTO can be operated as an ultra-fast thyristor with current-impulse commutation without a snubber, reducing the turn-off losses of the device to almost one half. The turn-off delay times are also reduced, and no minimum on and off-time is required.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The power conditioning system for the +/-8,5/17 MW-energy storage plant of BEWAG
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The electricity supply of West Berlin is operated by the Berliner Kraft- und Licht (BEWAG) and has been running as an insular system since 1952. In order to reduce the problems of this the utility company is considering using large-scale storage batteries in order to reduce cost for load frequency control and instantaneous reserve. The author looks at the design and some significant considerations when integrating a battery with an electric system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Field-oriented control of saturated AC machines
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A nonlinear field-oriented model is derived for saturated AC machines. The theory is applied to a field-oriented controlled induction machine operating in the field-weakening region where the change of saturation of the main flux paths plays an important role. It is shown that with the implemented current control, the control response is seriously distorted by the effects of variable saturation during field-weakening. When the linear model is used it is not possible to show these distortions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Designing a complete inverter system for a series tuned induction heating/melting load
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Although the series inverter has many attractive features it has not been applied extensively in the induction heating industry due to unexpected and/or unexplained inverter failures. The authors present a detailed, comprehensive and easy to follow design method for an improved series inverter which covers all passive and active components of the system. The inverter system consists of an input rectifier, an input filter of the inverter, the main inverter, the starting inverter, a blocking capacitor, a matching transformer, and a compensating capacitor. The design of complete inverter system is accomplished by designing each section of the inverter. For each section of the inverter, a step-by-step design procedure is given to select and rate the components. The design equations and curves of the inverter are presented. Finally, the use of design equations and curves to select the system components is illustrated by means of design example.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimal speed control of synchronous motors based on feedback linearization
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors propose a linearizing speed control of synchronous motors with constant excitation. The proposed control scheme involves, nonlinear feedback and position-dependent coordinates transformation, which decouple the nonlinear interaction between the d and q axes and takes a model of the synchronous motor into a linear time invariant system. A design method for a speed controller based on the linearized system is discussed. The authors apply the linear quadratic optimal regulator theory with integral action in order to obtain high dynamic performance. It is shown that the linearizing control makes it possible to utilize the advantage of the quadratic optimal regulator. The authors implemented the proposed control scheme as a fully digitalized software servo system by using a digital signal processor. The superior performance of the proposed control method is confirmed through experiments.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Redundant, fault-tolerant control system for a 13 MW high speed drive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Variable speed drives in chemical and petrochemical plants need a high reliability and availability. Therefore redundancy is often realized in the power converter and other subsystems. For the control electronics an interesting solution may be a redundant, fault-tolerant control system, which can reduce the probability of an outage by a factor ten. An additional man machine communication system with comfortable help information in connection with a modular control system can reduce the repair time of a failed control, while the drive remains in operation on the other control channel. The author develops this concept which is based on experience gained by Asea Brown Boveri.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An auto-adjusting PWM waveform generation technique
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A digitised strategy is proposed where the required firing angles or switching edge positions for PWM waveform generation are determined by an initial set of verifiable assumptions. A technique is developed, based on a matrix of transcendental equations, to determine the precise angles for minimum harmonic levels. The accuracy of the technique is shown to be dependent on the binary word length used in the microcomputer control process. A second stage in the development is to determine the energy spectra of the PWM waveform by means of Fourier transform analysis. A Fourier transform expression is developed where additional selected harmonics can be detected and eliminated with the use of a software filter. This renders the technique particularly suitable for its inclusion in a microprocessor-based high-speed versatile PWM drive system. The scheme can be shown to be auto-adjusting for harmonic elimination over a wide range of operational conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer modelling of GTO series strings in megawatt inverters
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: In order to study the effect of differences in GTO turn-on in series strings, semi-empirical SPICE models of the GTO and snubber diode have been used which were based on experimental data. The GTO model was derived using a two stage device/circuit interaction which is believed to accurately represent turn-on behaviour under these conditions. The computer runs have given useful quantitative data on the effects of varying turn-on differences, etc., on device switching losses. These results may be used to tolerance GTO turn-on characteristics and 'optimise' gate drive parameters in order to minimise turn-on switching losses. The modelling of complete inverters, consisting of devices connected in series to increase voltage capabilities, can give useful information on the operation of the circuit. Component ratings can be adequately assessed whilst reaching a compromise between solution accuracy and program execution time.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high current, ultrasonic GTO thyristor cathode switch
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The cascode switch, the series connection of a high voltage bipolar device and low voltage MOSFET, provides high power and high frequency in a small volume. The cascode switch has many advantages, reverse gate or base current is equal to the turn off collector or anode current level and can be established at a rate of greater than 1000 A/ mu s. The authors discuss a gate turn off thyristor (GTO) and bipolar transistor (BJT) cascode switch with similar power ratings of 180 kVA operating on a 500 V to 700 V DC rail and with load currents of up to 300 A. The circuit was developed for the BJT cascode or emitter switch operating at 150 kVA and 50 kHz and subsequently applied to the GTO cascode or cathode switch. The authors show the results achieved and compare the two types of switch.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new form of variable speed inverter drive for fuel pumping in passenger cars
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author proposes an AC invertor-fed induction motor drive for fuel pumping in passenger cars. The drive consists of a 2-phase invertor and a 2-phase squirrel cage induction motor with balanced stator windings. Its advantages are discussed and its performance compared with typical permanent magnet DC motors. An indication of cost, weight and volume of the 2-phase drive are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Interaction between the DC and AC side of twelve-pulse converter systems
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The twelve-pulse converter plays an increasingly important part in high-power electronics. The authors investigate the conditions under which the ideal twelve-pulse operation can be faulted. The main interest is focused on the DC link frequency changer with three-phase bridge basic circuits. It is shown that under certain circumstances for the ideal twelve-pulse action to be faulted on the AC as well as on the DC side, atypical harmonics for this type of circuitry appear. This investigation is based on computer simulation. The calculations were partly checked by empirical measurement.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Reswitching of an induction motor with remainder flux
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The behaviour of the remainder flux of an induction motor after a short supply drop-out and the reswitching with a thyristor switch is presented. The initial value of the firing angle of the thyristors is dependent on the value of the voltage difference between the phase and induced voltage vectors, in amplitude and direction. To measure the voltage difference vector the three induced and supply phase voltages are transformed to a synchronous rotating two axis system. The time function of the firing angle is chosen to be a linear function, the final value of the firing angle will be the phase shift angle between voltage and current.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Sliding mode speed control of a self controlled synchronous motor (SCSM) using an adaptive state observer
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Sliding mode speed control of a self controlled synchronous motor (SCSM) is presented. The states of the motor needed for sliding mode speed control, speed and acceleration, are estimated dynamically using an adaptive state observer (ASO). The widely known Luenberger Observer cannot estimate accurately when the system parameters vary. Therefore, good sliding mode speed control of the SCSM is not possible with Luenberger observers. However, the ASO used estimates the system parameters as well as the system states. It is shown that the ASO provides quite accurate state estimates, even when the system parameters vary. Therefore, good sliding mode control (SLMC) of the SCSM is achieved. The effectiveness of the ASO under varying system parameters is shown in the simulation results. The design of the adaptive state observer and the sliding mode speed controller of the SCSM is presented. Simulation results are given to show the potential of the control scheme.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Experience with large adjustable speed drives in power plants
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors discuss adjustable speed drives for power plant pumps and fans with horsepower sizes of 2000 hp to 7000 hp. They consist of a rectifier to convert 60 Hz power to DC and an invertor to convert DC to a full range of frequencies required to control motor speed. There is also a solid state microelectronics control system to adjust the frequency and voltage of the invertor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Development of a three-phase variable speed drive system for a battery fed underground mining locomotive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The development of a drive system for a battery fed underground mining locomotive and squirrel cage induction motor is described. The inverter, microprocessor and controller are all totally enclosed and the electronics is hermetically sealed against the harsh mining environment. This drive system is shortly being installed in a mining locomotive to undergo track tests. Load tests and heat runs have shown the thermal design to be adequate.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Investigations on a new electrical drive concept for the vertical axis of a selective compliance arm robot
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The new type of electronic commutated (EC) drive is a modern high dynamic servo drive. The authors discuss their use in the vertical axis of a selective compliance arm robot. Using Schroder's control method, extremely low pulsations of the torque occur and the power in the stator windings is minimized. It is found that the drive is ideal for robotic applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The development and performance of a digital subharmonic modulator for AC drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The subharmonic modulation process has been in use for more than twenty-five years with analogue circuitry and more recently using digital circuits which are not sensitive to offsets or drift to impair the fidelity of the output PWM pulse trains. The modulation process compares a triangular carrier waveform, quantised, with a similarly quantised modulating sine wave producing an output pulse when the two are equal, and repeating this to produce three output phases. The integrated PWM modulator, together with a microcontroller and a minimum of external components can provide a high quality motor current waveform. In simple form with linked voltage and frequency it is an economic solution to many industrial drives: with a control microprocessor it can also be used in flux vector controllers and complex closed loop systems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ultrasonically modulated drive system incorporating permanent magnet machine
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The combination of a rare earth permanent magnet machine and an ultrasonically modulated inverter produces a drive system which is both efficient, economical and flexible. The machine can be designed with a high power to weight ratio and does not need to be derated when connected to the inverter supply. Audio acoustic noise generated by the inverter is eliminated and the system is, therefore, suited to many applications involving quiet drives, in particular fan drives and ventilation systems. Other applications involve systems where a precisely controlled speed is required. Because of the use of a modular approach in the inverter construction the drive rating can be easily expanded. From a single pole module design an entire range of drive ratings can be produced and manufactured cheaply in quantity. The use of digital control for the system leads to greater reliability whilst reducing the controller costs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Convergence of rotor flux estimation in field oriented control
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors give a brief mention of direct air gap flux sensing methods mainly for historical reasons. They then go on to look at rotor flux linkage vector estimation using an open loop scheme in field co-ordinates. This method has some additional advantages if a field oriented controller is to be designed. The attention of the work is focused on the expected time constant of the estimation error. Finally, the study is completed by pointing out the advantages that the use of feedback in the estimation algorithm may bring in terms of the error dynamics. The results have been tested by simulation of a typical traction induction motor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New approach for flux control of PWM-fed induction drive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors present a comparative study of the different control laws of PWM voltage inverter-fed asynchronous drives and numerically realise one of these laws for the purpose of position control. Control is performed indirectly by means of a flux estimator, since this is not an accessible quantity. The principle of mode separation has allowed the reduction of the system order, and has therefore facilitated the implementation of the corresponding program on a microcomputer. Furthermore, optimum position control has been verified through satisfactory flux control. In this way it is shown that an appropriate flux control guarantees a satisfactory torque control, and consequently the traditional application domain of asynchronous drives is extended to other fields.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A highly reliable integrated magnetic UPS
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors present an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) based on an exhaustive study made to find the best solution to build a compact single static monophase UPS. The prototype had the following specifications: mean time between failures greater than 100000 hours, power range between 0.5 and 10 kVA and high static and dynamic characteristics such as cut time transfer less than 3 ms. The solution proposed, integrates four circuits in a unique magnetic core: the input network, two parallel reversible inverters which charge and discharge the battery and the AC output, with a series inductor integrated in the magnetic core.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent developments in the design and application of large, high performance cycloconvertor drive systems
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Development of high speed microprocessor-based controllers and their application to thyristor convertors, together with optimised machine designs, has led to an AC drive system which can meet the power and dynamic performance demanded of the most severe industrial drive applications. New degrees of freedom in machine/controller interaction and machine design have been established to enhance performance. Techniques have been developed and subsequently integrated to form a comprehensive software simulation package to optimise the design of cycloconvertor drive systems in terms of steady state and transient performance. Following a brief description of a typical drive system, the main modules of the software package are described and their interaction is discussed. Typical steady state and transient torque characteristics for a 6-pulse induction motor drive system are presented and discussed with reference to applications in the mining and metals industries, and applications demanding particularly low air-gap torque pulsations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Megahertz direct base drives for high power converters with high voltage bipolar power transistors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: In bipolar transistor converters two considerations are usually extremely important. These are low total losses (base drive and main transistor) and compact construction. These considerations first led to the concept of the compensated Darlington power switch, and then the concept of the optimized pulsed transformer coupled direct base drive. The authors discuss the topology of an experimental 1 MHz base drive. The unit is driven off a higher voltage supply in the primary, enabling the use of small FETs as drivers. They discuss the high frequency carrier wave system and then discuss the results of the system implemented in the prototype.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Three-phase transistor inverter for low voltage, high current, battery fed applications
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: AC inverters are increasingly being used for traction drives. The authors describe the practical development of a 3-phase inverter for a low voltage traction application. The practical prototype was designed for an 84 V supply with a 350 A peak sinusoidal current rating. The various aspects related to the power electronic design are discussed. Bipolar transistors were chosen for the main switching devices. Efficiency was the main reason for this choice, owing to the difficulty of cooling and the limitation on size in all the low voltage, high current applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Contribution to state control for elevator systems with respect to parameter variation and nonlinearity
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The demands on modern elevator motion control are the driving comfort, the precise leveling and the realisation of short running times. Starting jerks and parameter variation causes an uncomfortable run. By the means of a digital state controller there is a better chance to meet the requirements of a wide range of elevator duties. A compromise between costs and technical abilities leads to a solution with a minimum of actual signal detection and low effort on the drive system. Because of these points a control design implementing an observer and a disturbance rejection control is used. Besides this, the parameters of the linearized system are identified, thus allowing the observer coefficients and the gain values to be adapted. The authors discuss the results of this control concept and particularly the investigation of the parameter variation and the problems of nonlinearity of an elevator system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power device design for a hybrid actuator
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: There is an increasing demand for high current actuators with integral fault diagnosis. These can be produced using monolithic intelligent MOS based structures or by using a multichip hybrid. The authors describe an example of a two chip hybrid, high-sided, power actuator for 5 to 6 A DC current handling capability at 0.25 V saturation. The two chips comprise an analogue controller and power driver. The controller provides output, status, electrical and thermal protection and control functions. The power device is based on a high gain, low voltage planar PNP, with additional features incorporated for reducing the power dissipation of the linear controller and also for sensing thermal overdissipation. These features are included to improve the protection, feedback and reliability of the hybrid. The authors emphasise the special requirements of the power output function of the actuator.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A 20 kHz hybrid resonant power source for the space station
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A hybrid resonant inverter system is presented which satisfies the steady state operating requirements of a power source for the space station MSS (mobile servicing system). The steady state behaviour of the inverter is analyzed. A method to optimize the design of the resonant network is described. Finally, it is illustrated that the hybrid resonant inverter system maintains an excellent efficiency over varying output load demand.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some practical experience in the selection and de-rating of motors for inverter drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The engineer selecting an electric drive may only be equipped with general guidelines for selecting a suitable inverter and motor combination. The authors try to provide some guidance, gained from practical experience, on the selection of suitable motors and inverters and describe de-rating rules used by the leading UK manufacturer of industrial induction motors. The authors are concerned with drives rated up to 30 kW.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The characterisation of snubber diodes for use with high voltage GTO thyristors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: In a GTO (gate turn-off) thyristor the rate of rise of reapplied voltage during turn-off is limited by a snubber capacitor to avoid a refire. The capacitor stored energy is dissipated during turn-on by a resistor, which is then 'shorted' out by a snubber diode during turn-off. Thus during normal GTO operation the snubber diode is subjected to a successive sequence of forward and reverse voltage bias. The reverse bias results in reverse current being drawn through the diode as the stored charge accumulated during the on-state is extracted. The author characterises various snubber diodes for use in the protection of HV GTO-thyristors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application and control of brushless DC motors in high power robotic joints
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author discusses the application of a brushless DC motor to a high power to volume ratio robotic joint. The ease of application ensures that this type of motor will be more widely used in the future. The design discussed has a number of novel features, in particular the location of the motor in the cup of a harmonic drive. However the thermal characteristics of this design could pose a problem in certain applications without internal cooling. To date the prototype joint has performed to specification with few problems.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of a high voltage chopper for traction applications using two series-connected GTO thyristors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors study the principal dimensioning calculations of the different protection circuits and the snubbers of a single phase chopper using two series-connected high power GTO's. The experimental results obtained by this chopper loaded on an inductive charge are also presented. Finally, a brief comparative study of the different traction systems which are liable to be industrialized in the near future due to the recent progress in GTO technology is presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A high frequency resonant flyback switching power supply
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The advantages of high frequency operation of a switched-mode power supply are no longer disputed. This allows a significant reduction in supply weight and volume. However, high frequency operation has some disadvantages to the operation and efficiency of the system. The influence of parasitic elements (leakage inductance) becomes large, and switching and transformer losses (ferromagnetic losses, skin effect, eddy currents) increase. A significant solution to these problems is to use resonance to create conditions of natural commutation. Resonant switches (which combine thyristors or dual thyristors with a resonant circuit) allow spontaneous commutation and zero switching losses. The authors present a resonant-thyristor-diode for use in flyback convertor applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A transformer isolated AC to DC switch-mode power converter with resistive input current
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Switch-mode power conditioning circuits which provide regulated DC output power from utility AC input power while drawing resistive (or sinusoidal) input current have been developed for applications where harmonic current generation in the utility distribution and generation system must be minimized. The authors describe and analyze a switch-mode power conditioner which produces a 200 VDC output at 450 Watts from a 120 VAC (60 Hz to 40 Hz) power source while drawing resistive input current. A single switch-mode power processing stage is used which contains a transformer for input-output isolation and which operates in a continuous conduction mode.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An approach to filter design for UPS systems using PRM modulators
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Through an approach to filter design for UPS system applications, the authors analyze the capabilities of pulse ratio modulation (PRM) for the synthesis of sinusoidal waveforms. The results obtained point out the considerable advantages of this technique over traditional modulation techniques such as PWM.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimising snubbers for high-current emitter-switched transistors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors analyse a soft voltage-clamp to find a simple design procedure for optimising series-snubber and clamp reset-time circuits for a given voltage rise above the supply-rail. This analysis is applicable to other switches requiring voltage clamping rather than load-line tailoring, including MOSFETs. Their advantages of: reduced power dissipation over shunt-snubbers; current-dependent power dissipation, independent of supply-voltage; and absence of cross-current peaks in phase-legs are likely to promote continued usage.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-integrated brushless motion control system with digital position controller
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors present an analysis and design of a brushless motor motion control system having a lag-network in the current loop. A mathematical model of the current loop is proposed. With the use of the model, an accurate transfer function of the PI controlled speed loop can be obtained and a finite-impulse-response (FIR) digital position controller can be determined. The predicted transient responses of the speed and position loops compare well with the experimental results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Proton irradiated high speed SI-thyristors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A static induction thyristor (SIThy) is a semiconductor power device with many advantages. The authors report on the normally-off type SIThy with a surface-gate structure. The main current of a SIThy is controlled by a gate potential. At the turn-off process of a SIThy, the carrier injection from the anode region to the high resistivity region results to the tail current as well as GTO thyristor. Methods to reduce the tail current and to increase the switching speed are reported. One of them is the decrease of carrier lifetime with heavy metal diffusion or the use of anode shorting structure. A novel lifetime control method is proton irradiation in which a dual-sided proton irradiation technique is carried out to decrease the carrier lifetime locally and to increase the electrical performance of the SIThy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Demarcation problems in the engineering of drives for process industries
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The engineering of electrical drive systems requires the co-ordinated understanding of many engineering disciplines. In the process industry, the demarcation of engineering tasks in design groups requires a new approach. The electrical engineer has a role to play that interfaces with process design and also requires a detailed understanding of rotating equipment design, instrumentation systems and process control techniques.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An intelligent constant-flux AC drive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A new constant flux control technique for pulse width modulated (PWM) AC drives using conventional cage induction machines, based on observations of zero sequence harmonics generated by nonlinearities in the magnetising inductance of the machine is discussed. It achieves flux constancy within 1-2% for frequencies above approximately=0.5 Hz for both motoring and overhauling loads yet it requires no modifications to the machine. It is simple to implement with a microprocessor based controller and does not involve significant hardware costs or software overheads. Inverters based on this principle allow the drive's torque/speed characteristics to be accurately determined and in a prototype inverter such working variables can be downloaded over an RS232-C link to give a real-time display, on a low-cost computer VDU screen, of the drive's performance. The computer can also interact with the drive over the same link to give a programmable drive with data collection capability.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An algorithm for generating optimised PWM for real time micro control applications
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: In the reported literature so far, microprocessor implementations of optimised PWM for inverter-fed AC drives, are basically memory based. The optimised switching instants are computed off-line, using numerical optimisation methods and stored in the microprocessor read only memory (ROM) as look-up tables. The authors overcome the problem of large memory requirements usually associated with optimised PWM and also allow the switching instants to be computed online in real-time while keeping the harmonics distortion factor at an acceptable low level for three-phase applications. Fundamental voltages comparable to those achieved by the quasi-square wave mode are obtained, hence making it very useful at the upper end of the fundamental PWM voltage range, indeed it is possible to perform V/f control over a wider range. Also since the switching angles are computed online, steady-state as well as transient operating conditions are satisfactorily dealt with.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An integrated digital controller for brushless AC motors using a DSP microprocessor
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The recent availability of very fast digital signal processing (DSP) microprocessors provides the possibility of obtaining an all-digital control system-both speed and current loops-the AC drives. The overall integrated modular design should be more efficient, more reliable and certainly more flexible, provided the essential control requirements at least can be implemented in software. The authors describe the design approach and implementation of an all-digital AC brushless control system based on the TMS320C25 DSP microprocessor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulation of low voltage brushless DC motor drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A simulation technique for three phase brushless DC motors is described. The simulation method is especially suitable for low voltage DC drives where the motor and controller cannot be analysed or designed independently. A method of representing the action of the inverter using a system describing matrices is developed and demonstrated for one particular PIC. The steady state characteristics for the drive system are simulated and shown to be in good agreement with actual test results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Protecting a GTO under short circuit conditions
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: With the increasing application of the gate-turn-off thyristor (GTO), a need has arisen for improved self-protection under fault conditions where fast-acting semiconductor fuses are not available to fulfill this function. The authors investigate the design of the driver, snubber and protection circuits of a 25 amp 650 volt GTO used in a chopper circuit application. In particular they present a method of protecting the GTO under both accidental overload and short circuit conditions. Practical results are presented to verify the effectiveness of the system.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Measurement of techniques used in the study of variable speed drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The popularity of AC variable speed drives is increasing very rapidly. Measurement techniques that are used to investigate sinusoidally supplied motors are not always satisfactory-many instruments do not have the necessary frequency range to measure parameters such as voltage, current and power accurately. There is often a need to correlate many different parameters, for example to investigate the effect that the output waveforms of various different types of convertors have on noise and vibration. In many cases, particularly when measurements have to be made on site, there is limited time and access available for testing. Understanding is also helped by presenting the data in a clear and readable form. Signal conditioning, recording and signal processing equipment is described which enables signals to be recorded onto multichannel instrumentation tape recorders for later analysis.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Thermal modelling of high power GTO thyristors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The advent of high power gate turn-off thyristors, has led to high current and voltage capabilities at moderate switching speeds. Their potential use is limited by their inherent limiting junction temperature of typically 125 degrees C. This major limitation often leads to the derating of the device. The thermal modelling of the device heatsink system is required to predict the junction temperature under various operating conditions. The concepts of thermal resistance and thermal capacitance are no longer valid due to the complexity of the physical characteristics as well as the system geometry. A 3D finite element thermal model is developed to deal with steady-state and transient problems. The latter can be used to predict the temperature distribution under fault operating conditions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Instantaneous feedback in voltage source inverters: a comparative study between nonlinear and linear approach
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Voltage source inverters used in UPS systems feeding nonlinear loads must be capable of providing an output voltage waveform of quality in spite of all line and load disturbances. Switching algorithms applying output filter state feedback in order to control the instantaneous output voltage are discussed and two approaches are compared. In the case of the nonlinear controller, the driving force is switched at maximum amplitude into the output filter, while the linear discrete-time controller encompasses a synchronous pulse-width modulator placed in the feedback loop. The former gives a higher tolerance level to load disturbances, but encourages randomness in commutations. Simulations and experiments performed show that the latter combines both excellent dynamic performance and synchronous switching. Theoretical background and design considerations are included for both solutions.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Variable characteristic filters
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A novel technique for building variable characteristic 'active' filters is proposed. The principle of operation, methods of control, analysis and design of a typical active filter is presented. To assess the effectiveness of this technique, the proposed filter is used to control the input current harmonics in a phase-controlled converter. It is shown that by using a single filter a wide range of harmonics can be controlled.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Soft start of several large squirrel cage motors with one frequency convertor
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: In the LD plant number 2 of Hoogovens IJmuiden, Netherlands, iron is transformed into steel by means of 3 convertors. During this process large quantities of gas and dust are being produced, which have to be exhausted by using fans. The authors discuss the problems of switching of squirrel cage motor driven exhaust fans. The solution is to use a frequency converter for each motor, however this requires an unacceptably high investment. To solve this problem one converter can be used with soft-start equipment. The authors discuss the construction and components of such an installation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PWM-modulation of GTO-converters with a cyclic resonant snubber: theoretical and experimental limitations
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The spurious turn-on and turn-off of power semiconductor devices in converters, can be alleviated by the application of relevant snubber techniques. The operation of a resonant snubber circuit at approximately 100 kHz is described. The authors attempt to establish the trade-offs and limitations of this technology when applied to GTO PWM power convertors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Improved soft starter with thyristor chopper
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: An improved soft starter with thyristor chopper is presented. Different time varying functions for firing angle have been developed to speed up an induction motor with a chosen constant torque, without current and torque peaks. The firing angle functions influence the building up of the main flux, in order to avoid the normal transient problems. Simulation of the transients based on the analytical solutions of the machine differential equations for all modes of operation has been provided. The beneficial effect of the suggested switching functions in smoothing the transient flux, currents and torque is illustrated. Application of the switching functions has been performed with actual laboratory tests.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent development and future potential of the power static induction (SI) devices
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Power static induction (SI) devices, such as the power static induction transistors (SITs) and SI thyristors, have been developed since the 1970s in Japan. The power SI devices include the normally-on/off type power SITs and the normally-on/off type power SI thyristors. By utilizing the light triggered/quenched SI thyristors as a key switching valve for a long-distance DC power transmission line, a high-efficiency DC transmission system will be realized. 60 kHz, 100 kW high efficiency ( eta >90%) inverters, 20 kHz, 5 kW resonant DC/DC converters, 20 kHz, 100 kW PWM inverters and active filters etc. have been developed by utilizing the 1200 V-300 A class SI thyristors. A 1.5 MHz, 100 W class quasi-resonant DC/DC converter was also realized by utilizing the 1200 V-5 A class ultra-high frequency and very low-loss SI thyristors. The application fields of the SI thyristors are rapidly being developed. The development and the future potential of the power SITs and SI thyristors is described and the performance of the practically applied equipment is reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A snubbing and transient limiting circuit for inverter bridges
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: This new circuit uses no additional switched components to operate as a snubber at both turn-on and turn-off in a bridge circuit leg. The centre leg inductance carries full load current plus a transient for a few microseconds as it limits the turn-on current and dv/dt across the nonconducting GTO. This current stores energy which can be conveniently extracted for use or dissipation with a power about equal to that of the snubber capacitor energy.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High performance cooling systems for advanced semiconductor equipment
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Advances in efficient cooling systems for high power semiconductors are reviewed. These include processes, system schematics, advanced refrigerant fluids, computation methods and other aspects of thermal engineering in high voltage equipment.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Integrated digital control for drives and auxiliaries in the process industries
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Computerisation is a general strategy justified by the continuing fall in the cost of processing. The author describes how this gradual introduction of digital control has spread to all parts of process line systems and although gradual at a strategic level it becomes a step function to the people and equipment involved. First the separate building blocks are considered and then applications in two different process industries are described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Using variable-speed drives with 'sloppy' mechanical systems
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author considers the selection of variable-speed drives for use with 'real world' mechanical systems. The author outlines some of the problems that can arise, dispels some common misconceptions and suggests ways of finding out if imperfections in a drive are causing problems in a process. In particular he discusses the power converter and speed loop performances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Optimised power stages for high frequency 380/440 VAC medium power switch mode supplies
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors present the elements necessary to make the optimum choice of power semiconductors (for the transistors and secondary diodes) and the power stage configurations for medium power SMPS (between 1 to 15 kVA). The power stage realized comprises of an asymmetrical bridge forward converter. An optimised power switch combining bipolar and MOSFET technologies is developed. It is capable of switching in excess of 50 A at 25 kHz on the 380/440 VAC rectified three phase mains. Secondary diode choice depends largely on the transformer ratio and the desired output DC voltage. Conduction losses at 25 kHz govern the choice of secondary diodes.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Power electronics controls: specifications from the user's point of view
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The impact of power electronics controls in the near future will be staggering. The author present applications including commercial, residential, industrial and transportation areas. Also, some of the on-going research and development efforts of EPRI are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Screen inductance sensor for commutation and current profiling in electric motors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: It was the experience of the authors that no single commercially available transducer met all the cost/performance requirements of motor commutation. In fact the lack of suitable transducers has been a major obstacle in the development of the brushless servodrive. A novel transducer, known as the INSEN transducer, has been developed by the authors to fill this gap. The transducer is totally brushless and is characterised by its simplicity, ruggedness and potentially low cost. It is capable of producing both absolute position information and a high resolution velocity signal. Not only is it the ideal device for motor commutation but it also has applications far beyond in the general rotary and linear position/motion sensing fields.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Speed and flux control of a pulse width modulated current source inverter drive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A current source inverter (CSI) drive with high frequency pulse width modulation (PWM), which can be controlled up to twice the nominal speed, has been developed. These new PWM CSI-drives suffer from self excitation in the range of high speed. The controller developed avoids self excitation and controls flux and speed. For the fulfilment of this task, a state controller with a reduced observer is used. Simulation and good practical results of the investigations are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The future of bipolar transistors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The bipolar power transistor technology is in permanent evolution under the pressure of two important parameters: a request from power system designers for an increase in ruggedness (SOA, RBSOA, ES/B), an improvement in switching times, a decrease in drop voltage and easy to drive products; and the automation and control of wafer processing in order to improve the quality, the electrical parameter distribution, service and cost of power semiconductors. The author discusses the latest developments on the high voltage bipolar transistor model in the vertical and the horizontal parts of the transistor structure. Raw silicon and high voltage diffusion technologies are also studied. Some improvement possibilities, or a better electrical parameter distribution are also described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MOTOCONIC chip set: high performance intelligent controller for industrial variable speed AC drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author introduces the MOTOCONIC chip-set which comprises three VLSI devices designed specifically for variable-speed AC drive systems employing a 3-phase PWM inverter. As a complete control system combining both hardware and software, the chip-set is a more advanced version of the earlier hybrid devices that were developed by a systematic approach to the analysis and design of digital PWM techniques. A critical evaluation of the existing digital techniques is presented as a prelude to a brief description of the system development approach employed for MOTOCONIC devices. The system structure of the chip-set is described, and some experimental results indicating its high performance and functionality are given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor controlled synchronous motor drive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors describe a microprocessor-controlled scheme for an inverter-fed synchronous motor drive, particularly suitable in the 10 kW-100 kW range. A M68000 microprocessor is used to control a 3-phase GTO-based inverter and a switch-mode field feed system. The control scheme is based on the well-known self-synchronised principle, incorporating a rotor angle sensor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: PWM inverter with specified output voltage waveform using SI thyristor
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A new PWM inverter system with specified output voltage waveform is proposed. The inverter can be used as a specified waveform voltage source in any harmonic effect testing system of electric apparatus. The fundamental behavior and characteristics of the prototype PWM controlled SI thyristor inverter are discussed with the experimental and analytical results.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Stray inductances in GTO thyristor circuits
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Gate turn-off thyristors (GTOs) interrupt current at such tremendously high rates of fall, typically approaching 4000 A/ mu s in high power types, that the voltages induced by stray inductances as low as a fraction of a microhenry can be damaging. This necessitates the connection of a snubber network across each GTO, into which its anode current is diverted at turn-off. The authors present the results of a study into the relative importance of the various lumped circuit path stray inductances in generating these overshoot voltages. Mutual coupling effects are ignored for simplification.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Nonintrusive condition monitoring of electric drives and rotating machines
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: There are an insufficient number of faults for either drives and machines manufacturers or users to build up the experience to allow for instinctive diagnosis. On site maintenance regimes have had to be evolved in line with new working practices and reduced manning levels, so that plant personnel are not intimately acquainted with new equipment when it is installed. To compensation for this situation, monitoring and diagnostic systems can be built into drive systems to warn of impending faults and to locate and diagnose them. This philosophy can be extended to cover a complete drive system, incorporating electron controls, power electronics, electric motor, transmission and drive equipment. The author discusses the existing techniques of test instruments and nonintrusive condition monitoring.
