The concept of, and practical development of a self contained drive monitoring unit is also discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Constant current quarter bridge DC motor drive using PWM technique with a HIMOS transistor as a switch
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors deal with the design and implementation of a 300 V DC motor drive. The main characteristic of the circuit is the utilization of an ST-HIMOS (IGBT) as power switch. A short explanation about the physics and the structure of this new development in a silicon power device is given. The circuit simplicity and compactness along with the fact that it can be powered directly by 220 V AC mains makes this application ideally suitable for domestic appliances.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Operation of the naturally commutating hidden link converter feeding a cage induction motor
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors describe the principles of operation of the hidden link naturally commutating converter for the variable speed control of a cage induction motor. Initial investigations have shown that with direct converter-motor connection, the converter is naturally commutating for machine frequencies from zero to near supply frequency. The natural commutation of the converter feeding a lagging power factor load is made possible by an implicit frequency modulation of the output current waveforms. The associated problems and possible applications of the scheme are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Low-power controlled-speed drives using SR motors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors describe the operation and performance of small switched reluctance drives in the power range 100 to 3000 W with torques in the range 0.5 Nm to 10 Nm. The combination of a correctly designed SR motor with MOSFET or IGT power convertor and integrated control system produces a drive with excellent performance characteristics and which is cost-competitive with many conventional drives.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Voltage-distortion of current-controlled converters with DC ripple
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: In controlled power converters, the operating point is determined by the DC current mean value, which in the case of a DC ripple considered by the authors makes the precalculation of the main voltage disturbances somewhat difficult. Fundamental investigations in the time domain show the different effects of commutation and ripple. Based on an analytical description, the authors show that the time behaviour of the voltage disturbance can be derived piecewisely in an easy way.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Signal processing for determining flux and torque of induction motors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors deal with an indirect signal processing method for determining the flux components and the electromagnetic torque. The method utilizes the input voltage and current signals in order to obtain the derivatives of the stator flux. These derivatives are then transformed in the frequency domain by means of fast Fourier transforms and are successively integrated in the same domain. The implementation of the inverse FFT permits the flux components in the time domain to be determined and the electromagnetic torque to be monitored. The results are very accurate because the technique of Fourier analysis is the most suitable for examining signals rich in harmonics such as the output voltages of the inverters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A series-resonant converter used as an amplitude and frequency function generator
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A series-resonant power converter system is presented which allows generation of multiphase output voltages with very low distortion at high efficiency. The self-commutated resonant operation mode ensures the converter to be short-circuit proof. After a discussion of the control concept, some typical output voltages and efficiency measurements are shown.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Passive, microprocessor switch, and magnetic filters for power electronic drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Multiple converter thyristor drives in a power system must generally satisfy standard G5/3. The authors discuss the problem in terms of a 7 drive system with each drive operating an identical time-displaced duty cycles. Four methods of passive or switch-filtering have been compared in the context of a 14 converter drive in a food-processing plant. Microprocessor switch-filtering has been shown to be very effective, but sensitive to system disturbances. Magnetic harmonic cancellation in double-dual-converter drives is to be preferred if the correct firing relationships can be maintained by the central microprocessor.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The direct load angle control of a CSI drive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: There are many applications where high dynamic response, although desirable, is not essential. Such applications include many of the weight balancing and weight lifting drives. These drives operate with a gravitational loading applied to the shaft. Where a low speed operation is required such drives would benefit from the application of the PAM technique. The authors report on the digital implementation of a constant load angle control strategy, incorporating the PAM technique, applied to a stringent loading case. Novel aspects of the implementation include the calculation of the stator current reference as opposed to its formation by a conventional controller, while the inverter switching decisions are made with consideration of the predicted angle quantities at other possible stator current angular positions and their effect on the machine flux.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Starting of induction motors by static VAR compensators
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors propose the new thyristor-controlled static VAR compensator (SVC) be used in starting of large induction motor loads and to improve the feeding network voltage profile during the starting period. Superiority of static VAr compensator starting over the traditional shunt fixed capacitor starting is illustrated. The authors show that the SVC limits the voltage dips during starting, eliminates the overvoltages-resulting from its shunt capacitive part-at the end of starting, and minimizes both of the initial inrush currents and starting periods.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Soft commutation in brushless drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors study continuous speed variations in small brushless polyphase drives, fed by the commercial single-phase mains. They present the interesting aspects of the combined use of different types of semiconductor components within the same static converter. They show in particular how only one switch, equipped with an appropriate environment, can allow all the others to benefit from soft commutation conditions. The classical snubber circuits then become useless, and further, the electromagnetic interference problems are considerably reduced.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design of robust position servo of synchronous motors using sliding mode control
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors present a design method for a position servo system for synchronous motors with permanent magnet excitation by using sliding mode control. They aim to find a controller so that precise position control with desired fast response is achieved in the presence of variations of system parameters and external disturbances. It is known that synchronous motors exhibit highly coupled nonlinear multivariable control structure, which make it difficult to design a servo system with high dynamic performance. The nonlinearity comes from the nonlinear interaction between the currents of the d and q axes. The authors propose a method of designing a robust position servo system by decoupling the nonlinear interaction between the d and q axes with the use of sliding mode control. The authors implemented the control scheme into a simple model of a single link manipulator with the synchronous motor. The performance of the control scheme is verified experimentally.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fast high current switch for higher power switching power supplies
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: In a high power switched mode supply (SMPS) there is a need for a high power switching device. Generally three types of semiconductor switching devices are used in this type of application, thyristors, bipolar junction transistor (BJTs) and field effect transistors (FETs). Thyristors can handle very high power, but suffer from relatively slow switching times, and are generally used at frequencies below 10 kHz. BJTs with high power handling capabilities are also slow, particularly high current devices, and maximum switching frequencies are typically under 50 kHz. FETs can be switched on and off very fast and can operate at frequencies above 100 kHz. However, their power handling at high voltages is not as good as thyristors or BJTs. The authors present a technique for paralleling two low cost, medium power BJTs driven by a single low voltage, high current FET to form a high voltage, high power, high speed switching module.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor controlled inverter for UPS applications
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A microprocessor controlled PWM generator for UPS applications is presented. The method adopted for generating the PWM pulses is based on a combination of on-line calculation and look-up-table based data. A modular programming facility utilised to provide easy and efficient handling of the large quantity of look-up-table data. The simple technique used to eliminate the effects of interrupt delays, worked very well in practice and can be employed in three phase systems. The scheme used to generate the PWM pulses utilised only two mathematical operations. This allows the microprocessor adequate time to perform other functions satisfactorily, such as regulating the output voltage and implementing the phase-synchronisation technique, despite the relatively high carrier frequency.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluating the step response of traction VSI drive
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author shows that it is possible to predict the effect of the inverter input current transient by using a relatively simple analytical method which does not involve the time domain simulation of the drive system. The particular transient of interest is that due to the transition to the quasi-square wave mode. The analytical method described predicts the equivalent system eigenvalues bearing in mind that the system being considered is time varying. The effectiveness of this method has been demonstrated by comparing the calculated and computed (using time domain simulation) transient response parameters.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: MOSFETs and FREDFETS in motor drive equipment
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors discuss the properties of the FREDFET, a technology which yields a MOSFET with a very fast built-in reverse diode with properties similar to a discrete fast epitaxial rectifier. It is shown that its characteristics make the device an excellent choice for high frequency bridge leg systems such as 20 kHz AC motor control systems. Investigations have been carried out in dedicated test circuits as well as in a 20 kHz ACMC system which show that the FREDFET exhibits very low diode losses. It compares favorably with a discrete solution, using two extra diodes to overcome the slow speed of the standard built-in diode, and also with devices from the standard ranges.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Microprocessor control of a 3-phase to 3-phase 6-pulse noncirculating cycloconverter with alternative firing strategies
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors describe a controller which can produce the firing signals for a 3-phase to 3-phase 6-pulse noncirculating current cycloconverter using a dual-processor approach. A digital signal processor is used to perform the time critical task of generating the firing signals, using a sample based algorithm, and a conventional processor controls the bridge change-over process. The unit is compact and has been constructed on a single 6U Eurocard. Firing signals have been produced, using the normal control firing strategy usually used with cycloconverters, and also with controlled flywheeling which led to a reduction in output voltage harmonics, giving more continuous load current and hence an improvement in output waveforms. Controlled flywheeling also gives a significant reduction in the VAr required by the converter when operating at low modulation depths.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Recent development of the static induction (SI) thyristors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors describe two kinds of new SI thyristors. Firstly they introduce a new idea for an anode-emitter-shorted structure for the SI thyristor. The performance of the new anode-emitter-shorted 1200 V-10 A class buried-gate SI thyristor is described compared with the performance of the conventional IGBTs. Secondly, they describe the performance of very low-loss, high-efficiency, planar-gate normally-off type SI thyristors. The performance of the low-power class of the SI thyristors have been improved up to the extent that the switching frequencies can be increased up to a few 100 kHz accompanying with the ultra-low loss capabilities. In fact, the power conversion efficiency of 99% was realized at 100 kHz and even 93% at 1 MHz of the switching frequencies. The 1200 V-5 A class SI thyristors developed have been tested for the application to the quasi-resonant DC-DC converters. The power-loss of the SI thyristor was evaluated as functions of the switching frequency, and the operating temperature. The performance of the ultra-low loss SI thyristors as compared with the power MOSFETs in view of the operating frequencies and the power-loss capabilities, is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Inductive load switching measurements: realistic device evaluation
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Most power semiconductor manufacturers can provide performance data for even the most recently introduced device. This data will normally include limiting values for applied voltage, load current and dissipated power, together with selected dynamic switching parameters. As power semiconductors are applied in applications requiring ever higher operating frequencies the correct evaluation of the switching losses becomes of paramount importance. The author illustrates how the inductive load switching performance differs from that observed with a resistive load, and the extent to which the switching loss increases. Particular results are quoted for a 1200 V, 75 A dual, triple-Darlington power transistor module.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: High frequency power inverters for electric process heating applications
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The authors review the research and development work carried out at Loughborough into solid state power supplies for electric process heating applications. Further work is at present in progress to increase power levels and improve operating efficiency of the lower frequency (typically 200 kHz) units. In the higher frequency power supplies research into device packaging and high frequency drive circuits has increased operating frequencies and further improvements in the interfacing with microcomputers is also underway.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: New technology enables a breakthrough in DC/DC converter design
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Until a few years ago the DC to DC converter function had been implemented with discrete transistors and either separate voltage comparators and references or monolithic PWM controller integrated circuits. Being a leader in the power integrated circuit field, SGS-Thomson Microelectronics saw the possibility to integrate the various desirable functions into one monolithic structure including the power stage. The solution was provided by a new technology that SGS-Thomson was developing, called Multipower-BCD (BCD stands for bipolar, CMOS, DMOS). This technology combines low level logic and linear circuitry and power DMOS transistors onto the same piece of silicon. Multipower-BCD is a relatively straightforward 10-14 mask process utilising noncritical manufacturing techniques. The author discusses this new technology.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Applications of microprocessor controlled inverter drives
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author describes how users can gain advantages from using microprocessor controlled drives. The advantages include an improved user interface; advanced diagnostics; the integration of application solutions; and links with intelligent devices (computers and PLCs).<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Intelligent PWM inverter for induction motor control
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: Transvector control is an established technique enabling induction motors to operate in a wide speed range. The disadvantages of this method are connected with the evaluation or the direct measurement of the motor flux and with the sophistication of the required control technique. Starting from the 'field acceleration method' (FAM) suggested by S. Yamamura (1986), the authors have developed a new technique which employs rotor current feedback (FAMRCF) which simplifies the control system and leads to superior performance as compared to that obtained with other solutions. A new squirrel cage rotor current transducer was developed and the rotor flux was measured indirectly. Through stator current control the rotor flux magnitude is maintained constant and by accelerating or decelerating the rotor flux vector, the electromagnetic torque and consequently, the motor speed are easily controlled.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Computer-aided investigation of the turn-off performance of GTO thyristors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: A one-dimensional numerical model has been derived for the parametric study of the turn-off performance of gate-turn-off thyristors. This model takes into account all major physical effects and represents the interactions between the inner device charge dynamics and the operation of an external circuit. It is shown that, in spite of the one-dimensional simplification, this model provides an accurate description of GTO turn-off and can be used as a computer aid for circuit design and device selection as well as for device structure design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Spectral assessment of inverter waveforms
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author discusses work on a static frequency changer. Frequency plane analysis was used because it reduces computation time and removes cumulative errors that might occur in transient analysis. The author discusses invertor switching, the transistor switching function and load matching.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The practical application limits of very high power GTOs and very high power bipolar transistors
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: An overview is given of the practical application limitations of very high power GTOs up to 2500 A I/sub TCM/ and 4500 V V/sub DRM/ and very high power bipolar transistors up to 2000 A I/sub C(CON)/ and 1200 V V/sub CEX/. Some general comments are made about the limitations of medium power GTOs, transistors, Darlingtons and the combined MOS gated charge modulated devices (e.g. insulated gate transistors-IGTs). The latest ideas on extending the performance envelope of very high power GTOs and very high power bipolar transistors are also indicated. Because of the power loss dissipated in these devices which is often of the order of 1 to 2 kW when controlling high power at high switching frequencies it is necessary to use compression bonded double side cooled capsules or press packs for these devices. Not only forced air cooling, but also phase change (freon) and oil cooling may have to be employed to cope with this level of dissipation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Electronic control of power flow: present possibilities and some expected trends in applications
publicationTitle: Third International Conference on Power Electronics and Variable-Speed Drives
abstract: The author reviews the state-of-the-art in power flow control with reference to devices, topologies, theory, and notes on applications. The devices discussed are power convertors. The author then goes on to discuss the limitations of power electronics; switching losses and EM limitations. Developments in power convertor technology are discussed, particularly in the area of switching losses. Possible new trends such as medium frequency mobile power distribution systems and using electronic convertors as distortion compensators.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
